intro: Offices, teams, deadlines and meetings: the vocabulary of working on a project.
p.equipo.consejo: You say «trabajar en equipo». It is also a set of devices: «un equipo de música».
p.reunión.consejo: It comes from «reunir»: bringing several people together. You say «tener una reunión».
p.informe.consejo: You write it and hand it in: «redactar un informe», «entregar el informe».
p.cliente.consejo: It works for men and women: «el cliente», «la cliente»; «la clienta» is also said.
p.jornada.consejo: There is «jornada continua» and «jornada partida», with a long break to eat.
p.horario flexible.consejo: It goes well with «teletrabajo». The opposite is a fixed schedule.
p.teletrabajo.consejo: It comes from «tele-», meaning far, and «trabajo». The verb is «teletrabajar».
p.nómina.consejo: The accent marks the strong syllable: «NÓ-mi-na». Every month you get your nómina.
p.paga extra.consejo: In Spain many workers get two pagas extra: in summer and at the end of the year.
p.ascender.consejo: The e changes: «asciendo», «asciendes». The noun is «el ascenso».
p.retrasarse.glosa: to fall behind, to be late
p.retrasarse.consejo: It comes from «retraso». It is pronominal: «me retraso», «se retrasa». The opposite is «adelantarse».
p.cumplir con.glosa: to meet (a deadline), to comply with
p.cumplir con.consejo: You «cumples con» a deadline or a promise: «cumplir con el plazo».
p.contrato indefinido.consejo: It is also called «contrato fijo». The opposite is the «contrato temporal».
b1.titulo: Working life, from contract to deadline
b1.texto:
**Two ways of working.** **Por cuenta ajena**: you are an employee. **Por cuenta propia**: you are self-employed.

**In the office.** **El equipo**, **la jefa**, **el cliente**. **La reunión**, **el informe**, **el plazo**, **la entrega**.

**Contract and hours.** A **contrato indefinido** has no end date. The **jornada** can be continuous or split. Many companies offer **horario flexible** and **teletrabajo**.

**Pay.** The **nómina** shows what you earn each month. In Spain two **pagas extra** are paid a year.

**Moving up.** **Ascender** and **el ascenso**.

**Deadlines.** **Cumplir con** the deadline, **entregar** the report on time, **retrasarse**.
b2.f1.texto: The client wants the report before Friday.
b2.f2.texto: We can meet the deadline if we work as a team.
b2.f3.texto: Thanks to flexible hours, I start at eight and leave at four.
b2.f4.texto: I fell behind with last month's delivery.
b2.f5.texto: If you hand in the report on time, tomorrow you will leave earlier.
b2.f6.texto: The June payslip will include the extra month's pay.
b2.f7.texto: If the client is happy, I could be promoted.
b4.titulo: Llevar + time, desde hace and mientras
b4.texto:
**Llevar + time + gerund** tells how long something that continues has lasted: **llevamos dos semanas trabajando**, **lleva un año viviendo aquí**.

**Desde hace + time** says how long something has been going on: **trabajo aquí desde hace tres años**. With a date, **desde** is used: **desde el lunes**.

**Mientras + subjunctive** means «for as long as» and talks about the future: **mientras no haya un plan, seguirá el retraso**. When it talks about the present, the indicative is used: **mientras trabajo, escucho música**.
b4.e0.texto: We have been working on the project for two weeks.
b4.e1.texto: I have worked at this company for three years.
b4.e2.texto: As long as there is no clear plan, the delay will continue.
b5.f0.texto: At eight in the morning, the office buzzes like a beehive.
b5.f1.texto: The screens glow in the half-light like small blue windows.
b5.f2.texto: The team gathers around a long table covered with reports.
b5.f3.texto: The boss looks at the clock, breathes deeply and hands out the tasks in a calm voice.
b5.f4.texto: Nobody looks up until the coffee goes cold in the cups.
b5.f5.texto: At midday the client arrives with a cold smile and a grey briefcase.
b5.f6.texto: Pablo hands him the report and waits with his hands in his pockets.
b5.f7.texto: For ten minutes the rustle of the pages is heard.
b5.f8.texto: At last the client smiles for real and signs the contract.
b5.f9.texto: Marta closes her eyes for a second and smiles, relieved.
b6.o0.refuerzo: Yes: the client is the one who buys your work or service.
b6.o1.refuerzo: The boss directs the team; he is not the one buying your work.
b6.o2.refuerzo: A colleague works with you; he does not buy your work.
b6.pregunta: Who buys your work or your service?
b7.frase: Mientras no ____ un plan claro, seguirá el retraso.
b7.o0.refuerzo: It is indicative. Talking about the future, «mientras» needs the subjunctive.
b7.o1.refuerzo: It is future. After «mientras» you use the subjunctive, not the future.
b7.o2.refuerzo: Yes: «mientras» + subjunctive when it talks about the future.
b7.pregunta: Which form does «mientras no» need here?
b8.frase: Todo el equipo trabaja en el proyecto desde el lunes
b8.traduccion: The whole team has been working on the project since Monday
b9.o0.refuerzo: Retraso is lost time, not a direction.
b9.o1: Vamos más tarde de lo previsto
b9.o1.refuerzo: Yes: «retraso» is arriving or finishing late.
b9.o2.refuerzo: It is not about mood but about time.
b11.frase: Llevamos dos semanas ____ en el proyecto.
b11.o0.refuerzo: Yes: «llevar + time» goes with a gerund.
b11.o1.refuerzo: The infinitive is not used in this structure.
b11.o2.refuerzo: The participle does not tell of an ongoing action; the gerund is needed.
b12.o0: un contrato sin fecha de fin
b12.o0.refuerzo: Yes: «indefinido» means it has no end date.
b12.o1.refuerzo: That would be temporary, exactly the opposite.
b12.o2.refuerzo: Teletrabajo is about the place, not the contract's length.
p.trabajamos.consejo: «trabajar» means to work. The «j» sounds like «h»: tra-ba-HA-mos.
p.entro.consejo: «entrar» means to go in, and in offices it means to start work.
p.retrasé.consejo: «retrasarse» means to be late. The accent marks the stress at the end: re-tra-SE.
p.entregáis.consejo: «entregar» means to hand in. The stress falls on «GAIS».
p.saldréis.consejo: The future of «salir» adds «-réis» to the stem «saldr-».
p.llevará.consejo: The accent on «llevará» marks the final stress. It is the future of «llevar».
p.seguirá.consejo: «seguir» means to continue. Its future has the accent on the last syllable: se-gi-RA.
p.colmena.consejo: «colmena» is feminine: «la colmena». It is where bees live.
p.pantallas.consejo: «pantalla» is feminine: «la pantalla». The «ll» sounds like «y».
p.cubierta.consejo: «cubierta» agrees with «mesa», a feminine noun. It comes from «cubrir».
p.informes.consejo: «informe» is masculine: «el informe». The stress is on «FOR».
p.jefa.consejo: «jefa» is feminine: «la jefa». The «j» sounds like a strong «h».
p.reparte.consejo: «repartir» means to share out. The stress is on «PAR».
p.maletín.consejo: «maletín» is masculine and the accent falls on the last syllable: ma-le-TIN.
p.roce.consejo: «roce» is masculine: «el roce». The «c» before «e» sounds «th» in Spain.
p.previsto.consejo: «previsto» comes from «prever», to foresee. The «v» is pronounced «b».
